name: Bombs
description: You are given a permutation, $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$. Imagine that some positions of the permutation contain bombs, such that there exists at least one position without a bomb. For some fixed configuration of bombs, consider the following process. Initially, there is an empty set, $$$A$$$. For each $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$: Add $$$p_i$$$ to $$$A$$$. If the $$$i$$$-th position contains a bomb, remove the largest element in $$$A$$$. After the process is completed, $$$A$$$ will be non-empty. The cost of the configuration of bombs equals the largest element in $$$A$$$. You are given another permutation, $$$q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_n$$$. For each $$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$, find the cost of a configuration of bombs such that there exists a bomb in positions $$$q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_{i-1}$$$. For example, for $$$i=1$$$, you need to find the cost of a configuration without bombs, and for $$$i=n$$$, you need to find the cost of a configuration with bombs in positions $$$q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_{n-1}$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer, $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 300\,000$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq p_i \leq n)$$$. The third line contains $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq q_i \leq n)$$$.
output_specification: Print $$$n$$$ space-separated integers, such that the $$$i$$$-th of them equals the cost of a configuration of bombs in positions $$$q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_{i-1}$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
